title: Enterprise Onboarding: Health Checks, QBRs, Integration & Escalation Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Consolidated playbook for enterprise customer onboarding: integration checklist, support process, severity definitions, escalation matrix, known issues and workarounds, health check templates, and QBR agenda/templates.
content:
Overview

Purpose:
- Provide a single, repeatable playbook for enterprise onboarding that ensures a smooth integration, clear support expectations, fast escalation, and regular health/QBR cadence.
- Audience: Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers (L2/L3), Account Execs, and Customer Technical Contacts.

Scope:
- Covers pre-onboarding checklist, integration steps (API, network, data handling), go-live criteria, support process and severity SLAs, escalation paths, known issues & mitigations, weekly/monthly health checks, and QBR materials.

Owners and Roles
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (owner: Aisha Patel)
- Primary responders: Support L2 (rotation: support-l2@redwood.com)
- Escalation owners: SRE Oncall, Runtime Engineering, Security (as applicable)
- Solutions/Integration: Solutions Engineering (SE team)
- Executive sponsor/contact: Assigned AE/Customer Success Director

Onboarding timeline (example 6-week plan)
1. Week 0 - Kickoff
   - Deliverables: Kickoff slide deck, success criteria, primary contacts, timeline
   - Owner: CSM + SE
2. Week 1 - Network & Security Review
   - Deliverables: IP allowlist, TLS/KMS requirements, SCIM/SAML planning (if required)
   - Owner: SE + Security (if private deployment)
3. Week 2-3 - Integration & Test
   - Deliverables: API key provisioning, sample requests, end-to-end validation, rate limit confirmation
   - Owner: SE + Customer dev lead
4. Week 4 - Performance & Load Tests
   - Deliverables: Target QPS testing, latency measurements vs SLOs, batching config recommendations
   - Owner: Runtime Engineering + SE
5. Week 5 - Pre-Go-Live Review
   - Deliverables: Runbook handoff, escalation contacts, ops playbook, monitoring dashboards access
   - Owner: CSM + SE + Customer Ops
6. Week 6 - Go-Live and 30/60/90-day health check schedule
   - Deliverables: Go-live confirmation, post-launch review, 30/60/90-day QBR scheduling

Integration Checklist (API & Network)
- API Access:
  - Ensure customer has API key(s) with appropriate roles: "inference:read", "inference:write", "embed:read"
  - Example curl test: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
- Rate limits and quotas:
  - Confirm expected QPS and burst capacity. Default hosted tier: 50 QPS burst, 10 QPS sustained (modify via contract for Dedicated)
- IP and CIDR allowlist:
  - Provide customer with list of egress IPs for region; confirm allowlist or VPN peering
- TLS & KMS:
  - Confirm TLS 1.2+; for Private deployments, provide instructions for KMS integration (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault)
- Webhooks / Callbacks (if used):
  - Sample webhook JSON: {"event": "inference.completed", "request_id": "<uuid>", "status": "success"}
  - Ensure endpoint authentication (HMAC or mTLS) is configured
- Model selection and cost controls:
  - Recommended default models for first 30 days: redwood-rlhf-small, redwood-chat-medium
  - Recommend enabling token caps and rate-based alerts to control cost during ramp

Go-Live Criteria (minimum)
- All network and security checks passed
- End-to-end API smoke tests successful (>= 10 sample requests across typical payloads)
- Latency within SLO for typical payloads (see SLOs below)
- Monitoring dashboards accessible to customer and CSM
- Escalation contacts and runbooks exchanged and acknowledged

SLOs and Severity Definitions
- SLOs (typical hosted):
  - P99 request latency (prompt length <= 1k tokens): <= 1.5s
  - Error rate (5xx and 4xx unexpected): <= 0.1% per 24h window
  - Availability: 99.95% monthly
- Severity definitions (support response targets):
  - Sev 1 (Critical / P1): Production down, no workaround - initial response <= 15 min, engineering engaged <= 1 hour, ETA for mitigation/status update every 30 minutes
  - Sev 2 (High / P2): Major functionality impaired with workaround - initial response <= 1 hour, engineering engaged <= 4 hours
  - Sev 3 (Medium / P3): Degraded experience, non-critical - initial response <= 4 business hours
  - Sev 4 (Low / P4): Cosmetic issues, documentation requests - response within 2 business days

Support Process (How tickets flow)
1. Customer opens ticket via support.redwood.ai or sends email to enterprise-support@redwood.com
2. Triage by Support L1: confirm reproducibility, collect logs/request IDs, escalate to L2 if necessary
3. L2 investigates; if code/runtime bug suspected, create internal issue in JIRA (component: runtime-service) and assign to oncall or appropriate squad
4. If customer data or security impact is suspected, immediately notify Security and include "security" tag in ticket
5. Communication cadence: update customer at least once per business day for Sev2+, or per agreed cadence in contract

Escalation Matrix (contact & steps)
- Step 0 - Support L1 (support-l1@redwood.com): Triage, collect request-id, escalate
- Step 1 - Support L2 (support-l2@redwood.com; business hours): Deep investigation, apply known workarounds
- Step 2 - SRE Oncall (pager: #sre-oncall): For platform incidents impacting availability or SLOs
- Step 3 - Runtime Engineering (runtime-eng@redwood.com): For model/runtime bugs, performance regressions
- Step 4 - Security (security@redwood.com): For data incidents, exfiltration risk, or customer-sensitive issues
- Executive escalation: CSM will notify AE and Customer Success Director for any sustained Sev1 or contract-impacting issues

Escalation Playbook (Sev1 example)
1. Immediate actions (first 15 minutes): confirm incident, collect sample request IDs, place customer in prioritized queue and set incident label Sev1
2. Notify SRE Oncall and Runtime Eng via pager and Slack channel #incident-redwood (include request ids and sample traces)
3. Post initial triage (<= 1 hour): Provide customer status update with mitigation steps and ETA for next update
4. Mitigation and rollback: If recent rollout suspected, perform Canary rollback (owner: Runtime Eng) following rollback checklist in release runbook
5. Postmortem: Within 72 hours, produce incident report and classify root cause and action items; assign owners and deadlines

Known Issues & Workarounds (common)
- Issue: Intermittent tokenization mismatch in multibyte inputs
  - Symptoms: Unexpected token count, truncated outputs for some languages
  - Workaround: Normalize input to UTF-8 NFC and strip zero-width chars before sending; SE will schedule model tokenizer patch if reproduced
- Issue: Elevated P99 latency during sustained synthetic load tests
  - Symptoms: P99 spikes above 2s for prompt sizes >1k tokens
  - Workaround: Apply temporary request routing to Dedicated pool or enable KV prefix caching; reduce batch window to 10ms via service flag (ops only)
- Issue: Webhook delivery failures for customers behind strict CIDR blocks
  - Workaround: Use polling endpoint or configure VPN peering; add customer webhook IPs to allowlist and enable retries with exponential backoff

Health Checks and Metrics
- Weekly health check (owner: CSM + SE):
  - Metrics to review: 24h error rate, 7d trend in P95/P99 latency, tokens per minute, model-change events, billing spike alerts
  - Deliverable: Weekly health snapshot (1 page) posted to customer Slack and attached to ticketing system
- Monthly health review (owner: CSM):
  - Metrics: Availability, incident summary, usage vs forecast, capacity headroom, outstanding action items
  - Deliverable: Monthly health report and recommended configuration changes (batching, quantization profiles, model variant suggestions)
- QBR cadence and template (quarterly)
  - Attendees: Customer execs, CSM, SE, AE, Runtime Eng (as needed)
  - Agenda template:
    1) Welcome & objectives (5 min)
    2) Business outcomes review & success metrics (15 min)
    3) Operational health (availability, incidents, SLO adherence) (15 min)
    4) Usage & cost review (token consumption, model breakdown) (10 min)
    5) Roadmap & optimizations (batching, caching, quantization plan) (10 min)
    6) Open action items & next steps (5 min)
  - Deliverables: QBR slide deck, prioritized action list with owners and due dates

Templates and Examples
- Weekly health snapshot header (example):
  - Customer: <customer-name>
  - Date range: 2027-05-24 to 2027-05-30
  - Key metrics: Availability 99.98%, 7d P99 latency 1.2s, Errors 0.03%
- QBR slide checklist:
  - Title slide, success metrics, top incidents & mitigations, cost/time tradeoffs, prioritized recommendations
- Runbook snippet (rollback):
  1) Identify suspect release id
  2) Set traffic split to previous stable tag (traffic-control-cli set-split --service inference --tag stable=100)
  3) Monitor P95/P99 for 15 minutes
  4) Confirm customer with reduced errors before closing incident

Post-Onboarding 30/60/90 Checklist
- 30-day: Confirm baseline metrics, ensure all runbooks exist, any knowledge-transfer sessions completed
- 60-day: Optimization recommendations applied (batching, cache policies), initial QBR held
- 90-day: Evaluate contract for Dedicated or Private options if usage justifies, finalize long-term roadmap
